correctness.rationale: The synchronous update sends nonzero states up cyclically and the resting zero to 1 iff the opposite part is excited. A nonzero color cannot vanish before its forced procession ends; counting excitations over a periodic orbit enforces e_A(t)<=e_B(t-1)<=e_A(t-2), and the symmetric inequality. Periodicity then forces either both parts excited at every step (q-phase waves), exactly alternating active steps with an m-color two-step return cycle (2m phases), or no excitation (all-rest). Each nontrivial orbit requires full occupation of its prescribed residue palette on both parts, yielding surjection counts U_q and U_m; no lower periods remain because a progressing vertex visits each required color. The original proof gives these implications over all a,b,q. Independent complete functional-graph enumeration of 54 finite parameter triples classified 3434 periodic configurations and matched the formulas exactly.
residual_risks: The 54 finite functional-graph tests do not prove absence of longer cycles for arbitrary graph orders; the periodic excitation inequality and two-step return-map argument do.
Statement is for threshold one and the precise GHM rest/contact rule, not CCA or arbitrary graphs.
